reproduction_target: Downstream analysis of a single-patient seqFISH (Spatial Genomics GenePS) breast-core-needle-biopsy spatial transcriptomics dataset: on-instrument transcript decoding (Navigator, FDR 5%), nuclei segmentation (cellpose) and subcellular cell segmentation (UCS), H&E nuclei segmentation (QuPath v0.5.1), then a Giotto Suite v4.2.1 / R v4.4.0 pipeline comprising object construction and transcript-to-cell overlap, cell/feature filtering and normalization, PCA + UMAP + kNN + Leiden clustering, scran marker detection with manual cell-type annotation, marker-positivity quantification and spatial plotting, Delaunay cell-cell proximity enrichment, niche clustering by k-means on neighbourhood composition, spatially variable gene detection (binSpect) with spatial co-expression module clustering and metafeature scoring, and identification of interferon-responsive microenvironments with a 1000-permutation spatial null and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. All tissue collection, formalin fixation and sectioning, immunohistochemistry, clinical H&E staining, slide digitization and the seqFISH hybridization/imaging chemistry are out of computational-reproduction scope (counted in W).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from the Methods subsections 'seqFish workflow' (decoding portion only), 'Cell segmentation', 'H&E nuclei segmentation', 'Pre-processing seqFISH data', 'Clustering', 'Marker gene visualization', 'Cell-cell interaction analysis', 'Gene co-expression analysis', and 'Identification of interferon-responsive microenvironments within cancer regions'. Boundary call: the GenePS on-instrument image alignment and Navigator transcript decoding are counted as a computational step (C1) because they produce the transcript coordinate table that every later step consumes, even though they run inside vendor instrument firmware and are not user-scriptable; the upstream imaging chemistry and acquisition are counted in W. Clustering was split into C6 (dimension reduction + Leiden) and C7 (scran marker detection + manual annotation) because the annotation is a manual, non-scripted judgement step. Stage-1 prose-only: no code repository is stated by the paper, so no repo landing page or README could be read; no source was inspected.

steps.label: On-instrument raw-image alignment across hybridization rounds and transcript decoding with Spatial Genomics Navigator software, maximum false discovery rate 5%, on the GenePS platform (instrument set up per 'GenePS Instrument User Guide (INS-205)'); output = transcript coordinate table consumed by all downstream steps

Nuclei segmentation: DAPI images rescaled to 0.5 um pixel size, individual nuclei identified with cellpose (Stringer et al. 2021); no model name, no diameter, no flow/probability thresholds, no version stated

Gene-map construction and subcellular cell segmentation with UCS (Chen et al. 2025): 'A gene map consisting of all genes was created by adapting methods described by the UCS method for the transcript coordinates outputted by the GenePS platform'; UCS run on the cellpose nuclei mask plus the gene map 'as described'
H&E nuclei segmentation: whole-slide images from the clinical H&E digitized on Leica Aperio AT2 at 40x, nuclei segmented with QuPath v0.5.1 using the 'Cell Detection' module with default parameters

Giotto object construction and pre-processing (Giotto Suite v4.2.1, R v4.4.0): UCS masks imported with 'createGiottoPolygonsFromMask' and 'rescale', transcripts with 'createGiottoPoints', assembled by 'createGiottoObjectSubcellular', overlap via 'calculateOverlapRaster' + 'overlapToMatrix' + 'addSpatialCentroidLocations'; 'filterGiotto' removing cells with <25 unique transcripts and transcripts found in <100 cells; 'normalizeGiotto' with default parameters

Dimension reduction and clustering: 'runPCA' on all transcripts with default parameters, 'runUMAP' on the top 13 PCs, 'createNearestNetwork' on the top 13 PCs with k=13, 'doLeidenCluster' with default parameters, resolution 0.2, 1000 iterations, yielding 9 clusters

Marker-gene detection and cell-type annotation: scran 'findMarkers_one_vs_all' with default parameters ranking by transcript rank, then 'cell types were determined manually'; clusters 1 and 2 merged into 'Luminal epithelial cancer cells' based on expression profiles

Marker-gene positivity quantification and visualization: cells split into cancer vs non-cancer; unassigned marker transcripts attached to the nearest cell within one cell diameter; a cell called positive at >1 transcript per cell for the marker; spatial maps via 'spatInSituPlotPoints' with binary colouring; proportions computed over the cancer population; comparison thresholds ESR1/PGR >10% positive, Ki67 <17% considered low, against the patient's diagnostic pathology report

Cell-cell interaction analysis: Delaunay spatial network via 'createSpatialNetwork' with default parameters, minimum k of 2 and maximum distance 20 um; cell proximity enrichment via 'cellProximityEnrichment' with default parameters

Niche clustering: 'calculateSpatCellMetadataProportions' on a Delaunay network, 'getSpatialEnrichment' with default parameters for enrichment, then 'kmeans' with 6 centers and 100 maximum iterations; niche composition proportions computed over total cells per niche

Spatially variable gene and co-expression module analysis: 'binSpect' with kmeans binning on a Delaunay network, top spatial genes selected at corrected p < 0.001 and score > 1000; 'detectSpatialCorFeats' on a kNN network; 'clusterSpatialCorFeats' with k of 7; module annotation performed manually; per-cell module expression via 'createMetafeats'; per-cell-type contribution as the mean module expression within each cell type

Identification of interferon-responsive microenvironments: Delaunay network restricted to cancer cells at maximum distance 20 um, subnetworks extracted at minimum size 2000 cells, concave hull boundaries computed to delineate cancer portions, cells assigned by polygon intersection; interferon hotspots = cells with cluster metagene 7 >= 1.75 plus Delaunay neighbours at maximum distance 10 um, contiguous hotspots retained at minimum size 25 cells; enrichment tested against a null of 1000 permutations of randomly sampled spatially connected cancer-dense regions of equivalent size, quantified by z-score with Benjamini-Hochberg correction at alpha = 0.05

headline.static_readiness: 0/12 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: Under the most generous inference-inclusive reading, no step exceeds X at stage 1. Two independent hard blocks are in force simultaneously. (1) DATA: the article contains NO data availability statement, NO code availability statement, and NO accession of any kind - a full-text scan of the JATS XML finds no GEO/SRA/ENA/ArrayExpress/dbGaP/EGA/figshare/Zenodo identifier, no repository URL, and no 'available upon request' clause. The study is a single-patient clinical breast core needle biopsy, so the raw seqFISH images, the decoded transcript table, the segmentation masks, the digitized H&E/IHC whole-slide images and the Giotto object are all unavailable and, being identifiable human clinical material, would in any case require controlled access rather than open deposition. Every step therefore scores data=0. (2) CODE: no repository is stated, so nothing beyond prose exists. The downstream Giotto steps (C5-C11) are well enough described at function level - named Giotto Suite functions with most non-default arguments given - that a competent reader could rewrite them (code=1, reconstructable), but reconstruction is not reproduction and cannot lift a step whose data axis is 0. The strongest part of the paper is the VERSION axis on the R side: Giotto Suite v4.2.1, R v4.4.0 and QuPath v0.5.1 are exact pins, which is above the field norm; but cellpose, UCS, scran and the Spatial Genomics Navigator/GenePS software are all unversioned, and there is no lockfile, renv.lock, conda environment, container or sessionInfo anywhere, so version caps at 1 (exact_pins_partial, no environment closure) even before the stage-1 ceiling applies. Because the binding constraint is data-and-code absence rather than environment capture, a stage-2 code check would yield zero R-star gain; stage2_candidate is false. The realistic ceiling for this paper even after full remediation of environment capture is bounded by whether a controlled-access deposition (dbGaP/EGA) of the single-patient spatial dataset is ever made.
headline.coverage: 12 computational steps assessed from Methods prose. 7 wet-lab / instrument steps counted (W, out of computational-reproduction scope): patient consent and sample collection under BU IRB H-38024/H-38678; biopsy formalin fixation and 5 um sectioning onto the functionalized Spatial Genomics slide; immunohistochemistry for ER/PgR/Ki-67 on a clinical autostainer per ASCO/CAP guidelines (clones SP1, 1E2, 30-9); digitization of IHC slides on Leica Aperio AT2 at 40x; seqFISH hybridization with the Spatial Genomics Human Immuno-Oncological Panel on GenePS; automated 60x oil imaging with six z-planes at 1.5 um z-steps and iterative decode-probe hybridization / imaging / signal-removal cycles; clinical H&E staining and whole-slide digitization. NO data availability statement and NO code availability statement exist in the article - this absence is itself the dominant finding.

gaps.where: All primary and intermediate data underlying C1-C12: raw seqFISH multi-round images, decoded transcript coordinate table, cellpose nuclei masks, UCS cell polygons, the Giotto object / cell-by-gene matrix, and the digitized H&E and ER/PgR/Ki-67 whole-slide images
gaps.missing: The article contains no data availability statement at all. A full-text scan of the JATS XML returns no GEO, SRA, ENA, ArrayExpress, dbGaP, EGA, figshare or Zenodo accession, no data-portal URL, and no 'available on request' clause. Nothing that any of the twelve computational steps consumes is obtainable. The material is a single identifiable patient's clinical biopsy, so open deposition may not be legally available, but the paper does not say so and offers no controlled-access route either.
gaps.how_to_close: Add an explicit data availability statement. Deposit the derived, non-identifiable layers openly (decoded transcript table with coordinates, cell polygons, cell-by-gene matrix, cell-type labels, niche and module assignments) via GEO/Zenodo, and deposit the raw images and whole-slide images under controlled access (dbGaP or EGA) with the accession and application route stated. If deposition is barred by the IRB protocol, state that explicitly and cite the protocol constraint.

gaps.where: All analysis code for C2-C12 (cellpose invocation, UCS gene-map adaptation, the entire Giotto Suite pipeline, the bespoke interferon-hotspot and permutation analysis, and all figure generation)
gaps.missing: The article contains no code availability statement and names no GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Zenodo or Software Heritage repository. There is no script, no notebook, no parameter file and no figure-to-code mapping. The Giotto steps are recoverable at function level from prose, but the exact call sequence, the argument values left at 'default', the object state between steps, and all custom code (notably C3's 'adapting methods described by the UCS method' and C12's concave-hull / permutation framework) exist only as narrative.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish an analysis repository containing the runnable R scripts or Quarto/Rmd notebooks for the full Giotto pipeline, the cellpose and UCS invocation scripts, and the custom interferon-hotspot code; tag a release and archive it to Zenodo for a citable DOI; map each main and supplemental figure to the script that produces it.

gaps.where: Software environment for the whole pipeline (C1-C12)
gaps.missing: Exact pins are given for only three components - Giotto Suite v4.2.1, R v4.4.0, QuPath v0.5.1 - and there is no environment closure of any kind: no renv.lock, no conda environment.yml, no Dockerfile or container digest, no sessionInfo output, no Bioconductor release identifier. cellpose (version and model), UCS, scran, and the Spatial Genomics Navigator / GenePS instrument software are all completely unversioned. Giotto Suite v4.2.1 pulls a large transitive R and Python dependency tree (terra, sf/geos, reticulate, leidenalg, igraph, umap) whose versions determine clustering and spatial-network results.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship an renv.lock or a container digest covering R, Bioconductor, Giotto Suite and its Python side (reticulate environment, leidenalg, umap-learn), and record the cellpose version plus model checkpoint, the UCS version or commit, the scran version, and the GenePS/Navigator software and firmware versions.

gaps.where: C2 cellpose; C3 UCS gene map; C8 nearest-cell transcript assignment; C11 spatial co-expression; C12 interferon hotspot detection
gaps.missing: C2: no cellpose model (cyto/cyto2/cyto3/nuclei or custom), no expected diameter, no flow or cell-probability threshold, no 2D-vs-3D setting despite six z-planes being acquired. C3: 'adapting methods described by the UCS method' does not state what was adapted, nor any UCS hyperparameter. C8: 'within a one cell diameter' does not state the numeric diameter or how it was derived. C11: the kNN network for 'detectSpatialCorFeats' has no k; the number of binSpect kmeans bins is unstated. C12: the concave-hull implementation and its concavity parameter are unstated, and 'randomly sampling spatially connected, cancer-dense regions of equivalent size' does not define 'cancer-dense' operationally.
gaps.how_to_close: State every non-default argument numerically in a parameters table or, preferably, publish the calling code so defaults resolve unambiguously against the pinned versions.

gaps.where: C6 Leiden clustering, C10 k-means niche clustering, C11 binSpect kmeans binning, C12 1000-permutation spatial null
gaps.missing: No random seed is reported for any stochastic step. Leiden at resolution 0.2, k-means with 6 centers, kmeans binning inside binSpect, and the 1000-permutation null are all seed-dependent, and the downstream narrative depends on the exact partition (the merge of clusters 1 and 2, the identification of 9 clusters then 7 co-expression modules, and metagene 7 being the interferon module). Without seeds, even a correct re-implementation on the same data would not reproduce the reported cluster indices.
gaps.how_to_close: Report set.seed values (or the seed-setting code) for every stochastic call, and state whether cluster and module numbering is stable across seeds.

gaps.where: C7 cell-type annotation and C11 spatial-module annotation
gaps.missing: Cell types were 'determined manually' from scran marker ranks, and gene-module annotations were 'performed manually based on the transcripts found in each module'. No marker-to-cell-type assignment table, no module-to-annotation table, and no decision rule are provided, so the two most consequential labelling steps in the paper are unspecified human judgements. The interferon identity of metagene 7, which C12's entire hotspot analysis depends on, rests on one of these manual calls.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the full marker table per cluster with the assignment rationale, and the member-transcript list per spatial module with the annotation rationale, as supplementary tables.

gaps.where: C1 GenePS / Navigator decoding and the Human Immuno-Oncological Panel
gaps.missing: Decoding runs inside vendor instrument firmware that is closed-source and not user-scriptable; only the 5% maximum FDR is given. Neither the Navigator software version, the instrument firmware version, nor the panel gene list and codebook are provided, and the panel is referred to only by product name. Reproduction of C1 requires physical access to a GenePS instrument.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the Navigator software and instrument firmware versions and the panel catalogue number and gene list (or codebook), and deposit the decoded transcript table so downstream steps can be reproduced without the instrument.

gaps.where: Wet-lab and instrument acquisition: patient consent and biopsy collection under BU IRB H-38024/H-38678; formalin fixation for 7 h 40 min and 5 um sectioning onto the functionalized Spatial Genomics slide with 58 C drying and -20 C storage; ER/PgR/Ki-67 immunohistochemistry on a clinical autostainer per ASCO/CAP guidelines (clones SP1, 1E2, 30-9); IHC slide digitization on Leica Aperio AT2 at 40x; seqFISH hybridization with the Spatial Genomics Human Immuno-Oncological Panel; automated 60x oil imaging with six z-planes at 1.5 um z-steps and iterative decode/image/strip cycles; clinical H&E staining and whole-slide digitization
gaps.missing: Wet-lab tissue handling, staining and imaging chemistry are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W, not verdicted. Note that the single-patient, single-section design means there is no biological or technical replicate at any level, so the computational results are not statistically re-derivable from an independent specimen even in principle.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; the reproduction target is the downstream spatial analysis pipeline.
